newsitem.title: USA: DHL claims gains from UPS strike.
newsitem.headline: DHL claims gains from UPS strike.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said Thursday it has begun realizing long-term business gains as a result of the Teamsters strike at United Parcel Service of America Inc.

DHL, a privately held international express shipper that operates DHL Airways Inc in the United States and DHL International Ltd overseas, said many of the new U.S.-based accounts added in the last week are under one-year contracts.
Some of the new contracts include as many as 300 overseas shipments per day, it said in a news release.
After the first week of the UPS strike, DHL said it continues to experience a surge of incremental express shipments, with volumes at more than 40 percent above last year at this time.

DHL said it has made several adjustments to its network to accommodate recent additional volumes, including the acquisition of supplemental temporary aircraft and vehicles, increasing flights of existing aircraft and the hiring of additional temporary employees.
Because of the rise in volume, DHL said it has initiated several interim procedures to prevent disruptions to existing customers' business. The measures include:
-- DHL has temporarily suspended acceptance of domestic (intra-U.S.) business from shippers that did not have existing DHL accounts prior to the strike.
-- DHL will make only one attempt to deliver residential shipments, after which these customers are asked to pick shipments up at the nearest service center.
-- Drop boxes and service centers are still open to accept any international shipments.
-- As have other major carriers, DHL has temporarily suspended its service guarantee.
